name: Hungarian irredentism
summary: Hungarian irredentism is the political aim, dominant in Hungary after the 1920 Treaty of Trianon, of winning back the territories and populations lost to neighbouring states. It had an ethnic strand that sought the Magyar-inhabited areas and an integral strand that sought the whole historical Kingdom of St Stephen, and it asked for revision by diplomacy, the League of Nations and, in Apponyi's case, plebiscites.
scope: The interwar revisionist programme, as set out in Albert Apponyi's 1920 pamphlet and in the journal Magyar Szemle (1927-1944) as described by Caples and Pritz. It excludes Hungarian nationalism in general, the domestic politics of the Horthy regime, fascism, and present-day Hungarian government policy.
